Our framework introduces an explicit, structured user state 𝒯 \mathcal{T} (i.e., PersonaTree), thereby reformulating the problem as state tracking and state-conditioned generation. The goal is to learn a state update function f update f_{\text{update}} such that: where D t D_{t} denotes the current dialogue chunk, f gen f_{\text{gen}} produces the system reply given the current user input and the tracked user state, and f recall f_{\text{recall}} is a retrieval function that recalls relevant historical snippets from the full dialogue history H H conditioned on the current state 𝒯 t \mathcal{T}_{t} . At system startup, we construct an initial PersonaTree to serve as the starting point of the user’s long-term structured state. Specifically, we first determine the set of writable trunk and leaf fields according to a predefined unified schema, and constrain the storage type of each leaf node to a descriptive string, which is used to hold a compressed summary of the user’s core personalized attributes. This design ensures that memory capacity remains controllable and prevents unbounded growth as the dialogue progresses.
